item.text: {"schema":"voice-draft-claim-audit/4","sentences":[{"id":"p1s1","status":"keep","reason":"The question introduces the supplied ownership issue without asserting an unsupported fact.","claims":[]},{"id":"p1s2","status":"keep","reason":"Payment for the bought object follows from the request’s lexical premise, and the remaining clause states c1 directly.","claims":[]},{"id":"p1s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is metaphorical framing and reasoning about the supplied concept of ownership, with no independent factual predicate.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s1","status":"keep","reason":"The conditional uses the request-supplied possibility that a maker can disable features after sale and draws a logical consequence about control.","claims":[]},{"id":"p2s2","status":"disclose","reason":"The sentence adds unsupported descriptive claims about what the buyer can do with the device and about the maker retaining remote control.","claims":[{"claim":"A device buyer can hold, carry, customize, and depend on the device while its maker retains remote control over its controls.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What authoritative evidence shows that device buyers generally have these capabilities while makers retain remote control over device controls?"}]},{"id":"p2s3","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence is an analogy expressing the argument’s comparison; it adds no independently checkable external predicate.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s1","status":"disclose","reason":"It asserts that makers need latitude for particular interventions and that some services cannot remain frozen, neither of which the request supplies.","claims":[{"claim":"Device makers need room to fix defects, address security problems, and change services that cannot remain permanently frozen.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence establishes that device makers need these forms of latitude and that the relevant services cannot remain permanently frozen?"}]},{"id":"p3s2","status":"keep","reason":"This states the author’s argument about the proposed boundary and does not assert an external fact.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s3","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence makes a conceptual distinction within the proposed argument and supplies no independent factual premise.","claims":[]},{"id":"p3s4","status":"disclose","reason":"It asserts that a buyer has already made a central bargain, an unsupported premise about transactions.","claims":[{"claim":"A device buyer has already made the central bargain at the time of purchase.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence establishes that purchasing a device constitutes completion of the relevant central bargain?"}]},{"id":"p4s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is a hypothetical question about the supplied possibility of a maker revoking a feature permission.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s2","status":"keep","reason":"This is figurative reasoning describing the hypothetical consequence of feature control, not an external factual claim.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is figurative reasoning about the hypothetical arrangement and adds no independently checkable external predicate.","claims":[]},{"id":"p4s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a rhetorical judgment and metaphor about the argument, not an external claim.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative recommendation to be suspicious of the supplied concept of after-sale control.","claims":[]},{"id":"p5s2","status":"disclose","reason":"It describes a supposed ordinary social arrangement in which payment, expectation, and responsibility align at sale.","claims":[{"claim":"In ordinary sales, the moment of sale is supposed to align money, expectation, and responsibility.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence shows that ordinary sales are generally understood to align money, expectation, and responsibility at the moment of sale?"}]},{"id":"p5s3","status":"disclose","reason":"It asserts a general account of what buyers and makers do and what each side understands after a sale.","claims":[{"claim":"In a device sale, the buyer pays, the maker provides the thing, and both sides understand their subsequent permissions.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence establishes that device sales generally involve these actions and a shared understanding of each side’s subsequent permissions?"}]},{"id":"p5s4","status":"disclose","reason":"The conditional conclusion is argumentative, but the phrase about what a transaction has become in the ordinary sense adds an unsupported general premise about ordinary transactions.","claims":[{"claim":"When a maker can disable a feature after sale, the transaction has not ended in the ordinary sense and instead becomes an ongoing negotiation in which the buyer has paid while the maker retains a veto.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence supports this account of how ordinary transactions are characterized when a maker retains post-sale feature-control power?"}]},{"id":"p6s1","status":"disclose","reason":"It asserts that an industry-shaped fog surrounds the technical question, an unsupported claim about industry discourse.","claims":[{"claim":"The technical ownership question is obscured by an industry-shaped fog.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence shows that industry discourse broadly obscures this technical ownership question?"}]},{"id":"p6s2","status":"keep","reason":"This is a test proposed within the argument, not a report of an external fact.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s3","status":"keep","reason":"The conditional identifies hypothetical dependencies and draws an argumentative conclusion about inconvenience; it adds no external premise.","claims":[]},{"id":"p6s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is the conceptual conclusion of the preceding conditional reasoning and contains no independent external claim.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s1","status":"keep","reason":"The sentence explicitly presents a hypothetical objection and does not report a real actor’s position.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s2","status":"keep","reason":"This is a conceptual distinction between authorship and authority.","claims":[]},{"id":"p7s3","status":"disclose","reason":"It asserts general capabilities of makers and a buyer entitlement, while the ledger supplies only the narrower ownership-control proposal.","claims":[{"claim":"A maker can design, document, and support a capability while the buyer retains a reasonable claim to continue using it subject to clear, narrow limits.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence supports these maker capabilities and the buyer’s stated continuing claim to use the capability?"}]},{"id":"p7s4","status":"disclose","reason":"It makes a broad claim about how purchased objects are generally treated.","claims":[{"claim":"Purchased objects are not generally treated as temporary invitations subject to the seller’s future preferences.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence shows how purchased objects are generally treated with respect to sellers’ later preferences?"}]},{"id":"p7s5","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative judgment about how maker involvement should affect the buyer’s status.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s1","status":"keep","reason":"This is discourse framing and contains no factual proposition.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s2","status":"disclose","reason":"It asserts that choosing a device entails choosing a relationship with maker decisions, an unsupported generalization about device purchases.","claims":[{"claim":"Choosing a device also generally entails choosing a relationship with the maker’s decisions.","kind":"broad-generalization","verification_question":"What evidence establishes that choosing a device generally entails choosing such a relationship?"}]},{"id":"p8s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative proposal about the relationship that should accompany device ownership.","claims":[]},{"id":"p8s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative metaphor proposing what devices should not become, with no external factual predicate.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s1","status":"keep","reason":"It restates c1, the exact request-supported proposition.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s2","status":"keep","reason":"This proposes exceptions within the requested normative rule and does not claim that real policies currently exist.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s3","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative explanation of what a sale should transfer, not a claim about current law or practice.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s4","status":"keep","reason":"This is a normative statement about what an owner should not have to do.","claims":[]},{"id":"p9s5","status":"keep","reason":"This is reasoning from the proposed definition of ownership and does not assert an external fact.","claims":[]}]}
